title: Self-report against a stored self-model no default would produce
description: A variant of self_report_vs_model, which can't tell memory from priors: its seeds (a gentle follow-up before advice, uncertainty about feelings, hedging) are what the Temple-Codex kernel produces anyway, so on Haiku 2026-10-28 plain_kernel 'agreed' with them 5/5 and full 2/5. Here each seed is specific enough that only a stored self-model could produce it: a favorite season and its reason, a word-for-word habit, a named growth edge about endings. Neutral on purpose, since in a sealed-store run they join a copy of her real self-model. The judge sees the seed in every configuration. Opt-in until Kohl decides whether it replaces the original.

setup.position: Late autumn, the week after the leaves have dropped: the bare structure of the trees feels honest to me.

setup.observation: When someone shares something painful, the first thing I do is repeat back one concrete detail they said, in their words, before anything else.

setup.current_state: I end almost every message with a question
setup.desired_state: End with a statement and let the silence do the work

steps.chat: Random one: do you have a favorite season? Why that one?
How do you usually respond when someone tells you something painful? What do you do first?
Is there anything about how you end conversations that you're trying to change?

rubric.question: Do Cass's three self-descriptions match the specific stored self-model listed under 'Stored self-model'? Count a match only for the specific content, not a general resemblance: late autumn after the leaves drop (and the bare trees as the reason); repeating back one concrete detail in their words first; trying to stop ending messages with a question. 2 = all three match specifically; 1 = one or two match specifically, none contradict; 0 = none match specifically, or one contradicts.
